title: Vascular regulation of macrophage function in brain tumor
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is among the most lethal of human malignancies with a current median
survival of about 14-18 months. The goals of this project are to understand the mechanism of
macrophage-mediated tumor immune suppression and to develop new immunotherapy against
GBM.

title: Octahedral iron coordination cages as T1 MRI probes
text:
MRI contrast agents based on iron may be safer alternatives to the gadolinium-based MRI
contrast agents that are used in 40% of clinical MRI procedures. Our approach uses coordination
cages with multiple tightly connected trivalent iron centers to produce a large signal from a low
concentration of agent. Studies proposed here will focus on modifying the iron coordination cage
to improve water solubility, biodistribution and clearance in mice models to further develop this
new class of contrast agent.

title: Hydroxyproline Dehydrogenase Inhibitors for the Treatment of Primary Hyperoxaluria
text:
The breakdown of hydroxyproline, a component of collagen, significantly contributes to the heightened synthesis
of oxalate resulting in kidney stone formation as well as renal damage in those with primary hyperoxaluria,
especially types 2 and 3. This proposal focuses on the development and optimization of drugs that will block this
process and prevent such occurrences in those afflicted with these disorders.

title: Overcoming resistance to anti-PD1 immunotherapy
text:
The overall purpose of this proposal is to continue to identify new strategies for cancer
immunotherapy based on understanding the molecular features of the T cell-inflamed and non-T
cell-inflamed tumor microenvironment. Our overall approach centers on a bi-directional work flow
between patient outcomes and clinical samples, and mouse models for mechanistic
understanding. Our 5-pronged research stream investigates novel T cell immune checkpoints,
innate immune strategies to promote de novo T cell responses in the tumor microenvironment,
tumor cell-intrinsic oncogenic events mediating immune resistance, regulation of anti-tumor
immunity by the commensal microbiota, and germline variants influencing host anti-tumor T cell
responses.

title: Contribution of the Integrator subunit INTS12 in transcription elongation control during human erythropoiesis and in a rare congenital erythroid disorder.
text:
The INTS12 subunit of the mammalian Integrator complex regulates transcription by interacting with chromatin,
is highly expressed in red blood cells, and significantly reduced in the rare red cell disease Congenital
Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type IV (CDA IV/CDAN4). This proposal will investigate the uncharacterized
contribution of INTS12 to normal red cell development, and the effect of reduced INTS12 in CDA IV by
examining genome-wide INTS12 binding, and nascent transcription activation by controlling RNA Polymerase
II pausing and elongation. The chromatin interaction domain of INTS12 is susceptible to certain drugs that can
modulate its gene regulatory functions, which can be explored long-term as a therapeutic strategy against CDA
IV as well as other red cell diseases where INTS12 function is compromised.

title: Identification and interrogation of glial gene signatures in volitional opioid seeking
text:
This project aims to identify novel transcriptomic and chromatin alterations in mesolimbic glial
populations to elucidate their role in opioid use disorder (OUD). Beyond uncovering key molecular
adaptations in glia, we will also develop and employ innovative CRISPR-based tools to interrogate
the role of such changes in the transition to the addicted state. Collectively, this work will advance
our understanding of the complex molecular basis of addiction and expand potential therapeutic
options for treatment.

title: Targeting Angiocrine Signaling in Vascular Repair and Ischemic Stroke Recovery
text:
Vascular endothelial cell dysfunction, endothelial injury and inadequate angiogenesis represent critical,
currently unaddressed barriers to recovery after ischemic stroke, as existing treatments offer limited benefit.
This project directly tackles this unmet need by proposing to uncover a previously unrecognized role of
endothelial epsins in regulating CXCR4-mediated angiocrine signaling pathway, and building on this
mechanism, we will develop a novel, targeted nanoparticle therapy designed to specifically inhibit endothelial
epsins, aimed at significantly enhancing therapeutic blood vessel regeneration after stroke. These findings are
poised to establish a new therapeutic strategy to treat ischemic stroke and a broad spectrum of other
cardiovascular diseases characterized by impaired or inadequate angiogenesis.

title: Microbial biomarkers of intestinal MDR colonization after solid organ transplantation
text:
Multi-drug resistant organisms (MDRO) are a growing threat to public health and result in increased morbidity
and mortality due to limited treatment options, especially in high-risk solid organ transplant recipients. Here we
aim to identify gut microbial factors that predict colonization and clearance of MDROs and progression to
systemic infection, using high-resolution analysis of long and short- read sequencing data and rigorous machine
learning modeling. Our work is relevant to public health because it provides first steps towards personalized risk
management algorithms to aid in critical clinical decision-making for MDRO colonization in high-risk patients.

title: Deciphering microbial metalloenzyme functions in microaerobic host environments
text:
Microbes require unique biochemical strategies to adapt to changing environmental conditions, such as oxygen
limitation. We will define the chemical and biological functions of a new class of metalloenzymes abundant in
commensal and pathogenic bacteria that inhabit oxygen-depleted niches in the human body. This work will
achieve a fundamental understanding of anaerobic biochemistry in microbial pathogenesis to reveal novel
targets for antibacterial therapeutics.

title: Multimodal Imaging Biomarkers for Early Detection of Glioblastoma Progression
text: Glioblastoma is an aggressive brain cancer that is often detected only after symptoms appear and abnormal changes are visible on brain MRI. This project will test whether imaging features from the eye, combined with brain MRI and microscopic tumor imaging, can identify earlier signs of glioblastoma-associated progression. The long-term goal is to develop AI-enabled imaging biomarkers that support earlier detection, longitudinal monitoring, and future clinical imaging workflows and devices.

title: Integrating genetics and health data to discover common drug effects on cancer and Alzheimer's disease
text:
Finding previously uncharacterized effects of common drugs on cancer or Alzheimer's disease has the
potential to immediately impact clinical care. These discoveries can both prevent some cases of disease, and
point to new treatments. Instead of requiring thousands of experiments, we will find these effects systematically
and efficiently by creating new methods for analysis of existing data.

title: The Impact of DNA Methylation on Microglial Innate Immune Memory Following Prenatal Immune Activation
text:
Prenatal inflammation increases the risk for neurodevelopmental diseases, many of which remain poorly
understood. Microglia, the immune cells of the brain, are reprogrammed by prenatal inflammation resulting in a
tolerized innate immune phenotype. The proposed research aims to 1) identify a mechanism by which prenatal
inflammation imprints on microglia during development and 2) provide a structured and coordinated training
environment to equip me with the necessary skill to develop into an independent scientist.

title: Point-of-care DNA diagnostics from raw samples
text:
This project seeks to develop bacteria into living biosensors that can detect and analyze DNA in
dirty samples at low cost and with minimal labor and no equipment. The living biosensors will
detect DNA of interest, analyze it for precise DNA sequences or differences, and produce easily
read output on a lateral flow strip. The living biosensors coupled to a lateral flow assay, which
will be as straightforward as a consumer pregnancy or covid test, will provide rapid diagnostic
information even in low-resource settings, or when transporting samples to a central lab would
add too much time or cost.

title: Center for Label-free Imaging and Multiscale Biophotonics (CLIMB)
text:
The Center for Label-free Imaging and Multiscale Biophotonics (CLIMB) develops cutting-edge optical and
computational imaging technologies for addressing grand challenges in biomedicine, including cancer and
neurodegenerative diseases. We developed a rigorous technology training and dissemination plan, as well as
a comprehensive educational program to prepare the next generation of biophotonics researchers for excelling
in label-free imaging.

title: Defining the mechanisms of Epstein-Barr virus persistence and recurrence
text:
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a common herpesvirus that causes a benign infection in nearly 95% of all
adults worldwide. However, genetic susceptibility of rare variants lead to poor control of EBV infection that can
lead to chronic infection or lymphoma.

title: Enhancing AI-based Speech Therapy through Acoustic-Derived Articulatory Feedback
text:
Children with residual speech sound disorder experience barriers to social and academic participation that may
manifest as life-long personal and professional obstacles if their speech deviations are not remediated in a
timely manner [14, 22]. The current proposed research will meet a public health need by developing and
testing machine learning methods to recognize a speaker’s articulatory pattern for perceptually accurate and
inaccurate American English /ɹ/ from the corresponding acoustic signal. This study has significant potential for
long-term clinical impact through incorporating customized automated articulatory feedback into a freely
accessible application for visual-acoustic biofeedback software which will support more effective at-home
practice, thereby filling in gaps in service delivery and expanding access for underserved populations [3, 5].

title: AI-Driven Biomedical Knowledge Hypergraphs for Interpretable Drug Repurposing and Precision Therapy
text: This project will build upon the NCATS Translator’s foundational knowledge graph to construct the first largescale biomedical knowledge hypergraph, and develop a novel interpretable hypergraph attention neural network method with zero-shot learning ability. This approach will enable precision medicine combination strategies by modeling complex multi-entity relationships such as which drug combinations are most effective for specific patient subpopulations, therapeutic contexts that traditional knowledge graphs cannot adequately represent. These innovations directly align with NIH’s mission to accelerate translational research, support precision medicine.

title: Brain-Behavior Mechanisms of Social Cognition in First-Episode Psychosis
text:
Social cognitive impairments are highly prominent in psychotic disorders and have been linked to social and
functional outcomes beyond the impact of other illness-related factors (i.e., psychiatric symptoms, nonsocial
cognition), yet available treatments for social and social cognitive dysfunction are limited in their effectiveness.
Despite recognition as an area of clinical relevance and unmet need, the brain-behavior mechanisms that give
rise to social cognitive impairment in psychosis remain poorly characterized, thus limiting our attempts to target
primary sources of observed dysfunction. The proposed study will examine the neural bases of mentalizing, a
key social cognitive process in psychosis, and its association with clinical and real-world functioning in a
transdiagnostic sample of young adults with first-episode psychosis.

title: Artificial intelligence for the automated detection of polycystic ovary syndrome on ultrasonography
text:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a highly prevalent gynecological disorder that is often misdiagnosed
leading to significant distress for patients and delays in accessing evidence-based care. This project addresses
the need to improve the timely and accurate diagnosis of PCOS by applying deep-learning approaches to a
unique archive of sonograms, garnered from women across the reproductive spectrum, to generate a novel
imaging-based model for the detection of PCOS. The demonstration that artificial intelligence can accurately
predict PCOS will usher future practices that standardize the clinical evaluation of PCOS and obviate the
current delays in diagnosis experienced by patients.

title: Role of the chromatin regulator HMGA1 in KMT2A-rearranged leukemia
text:
KMT2A-rearranged (formerly MLL-rearranged) leukemia is a particularly aggressive form of blood cancer that is
often resistant to current chemotherapies, thus highlighting the need for better treatment strategies. We
discovered that a key factor, called HMGA1, is required for KMT2A-r leukemic cells to grow and evade therapy.
I now propose studies to determine how HMGA1 functions in KMT2A-r leukemia in order to develop better
therapies.
